samples.summary: `--dry-run` bypasses the new one-segment encoding and the `.`/`..` refusal, printing a traversal URL as "the request that would be sent"
samples.evidence:
The delta documents (docs/design/cli.md §10 additions) that every id the client interpolates is percent-encoded by `seg()` and that a `.`/`..` id is refused with exit 1 "before any request is sent". That guarantee lives only in `HttpClient` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:71-76). The second, parallel URL builder — `printDryRun` (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:13) — interpolates `config.workspace` and the caller-built `path` raw:

  const url = `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}`;

and every command builds that `path` from raw argv ids and returns *before* the client is ever touched: `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:52-58` (`/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tab}/cells/${ref}`), `cells.ts:85-90`, `cells.ts:133-139`, `tabs.ts:48`, `tabs.ts:72`, `sheets-import.ts:84`, `notes.ts:94`, `notes.ts:112`, `notes.ts:140`, `files.ts:63`, `files.ts:123`, `files.ts:141`, `docs.ts:134`.

Attack/exposure: `wafflebase sheets cells set '../../../../workspaces/other-ws/api-keys/key-1' A1 x --dry-run` exits 0 and prints `"url": "https://api…/api/v1/workspaces/ws-1/documents/../../../../workspaces/other-ws/api-keys/key-1/tabs/…"`, and `--workspace ..` / a doc id of `..` is likewise not refused here (no `seg()` call in this file at all). docs/design/cli.md:815-826 promises dry-run "prints the request that would be sent", and the CLI is explicitly aimed at agents (docs/design/cli.md:22-26), which are the consumers most likely to take the printed URL and run it through `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer …"` — executing exactly the out-of-base request, with the session's bearer token and the command's method, that `seg()` was added to prevent. Even absent that, the preview now misreports the request: the real send would either 404 on an escaped literal id or throw `Invalid path segment`.

Fix is one line: route the dry-run URL through the same `seg()` (export it) so preview and send agree, and so the dot-segment refusal fires on the dry-run path too.

samples.summary: No test covers the dry-run URL builder against the traversal ids the new §10 text claims are pinned, so the bypass reads as covered
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:493-561` exercises the traversal cases only through `HttpClient` (`deleteDocument`, `setCell`, `renameTab`, workspace via constructor, and the `.`/`..` refusal). Greps for `printDryRun` / `dry_run` / `Invalid path segment` across packages/cli/test turn up no assertion on `packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts`, and grep for `seg(` shows the helper is module-private to http-client.ts, so nothing else can reuse it. The result is a green suite that asserts the documented one-segment property on one of the two URL builders while the other (the one whose output an agent copy-pastes) is unconstrained — the added-but-bypassable-gate pattern, where the docs and tests both read as covered.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described and is reachable. packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:13 interpolates `config.workspace` and the caller-built `path` raw into the URL, with no `seg()` call anywhere in the file, while the parallel builder in HttpClient percent-encodes every id and refuses `.`/`..` (http-client.ts:71-76, :108, :239-434). The dry-run branches in cells.ts:51-59, :84-91, :132-140 and tabs.ts:47-50, :71-76 pass raw commander positionals/options and `return` before any client is built, and root.ts:24-40/:66 performs no id or workspace validation, so no upstream guard makes it unreachable. Result: the preview emits a dot-segment-resolvable, out-of-base URL for input that the real send path would refuse — a divergence in a path-traversal guard, in an agent-targeted CLI whose docs promise the printed URL is "the request that would be sent" (docs/design/cli.md:815-816, :22-26). I could not refute on not-present, already-guarded, or unreachability; the only doubt is impact (no fetch is issued from this path), which is not sufficient to drop a traversal-guard gap from the security gate.
